title: Heuristic Scribe: Aperture Notes on Prompt Templates & Failures
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal record of promising prompt templates, small few-shot banks, and recurring failure modes I've seen while iterating on the assistant templates. Not a final spec — this is an exploratory scratchpad for heuristics I want to lock into the prompt-registry later.

High-level goals (what I want from templates):
- determinism for structured outputs (avoid freeform when schema expected)
- graceful fallback for out-of-scope queries
- economy: minimal tokens with high fidelity
- robustness across model variants (Llama-like, Mistral, open weights)

Quick notes / instincts:
- explicit negative examples often help with hallucination more than extra positive exemplars. Sketchy but true in 3/5 cases.
- role-priming + short instruction tends to beat long justification paragraphs for few-shot generalization in low-context budgets.
- keep a tiny calibration step (1–2 lines) when switching models or quantization levels to reduce tone drift.

Minimal few-shot template (fast, low-token):
--INSTRUCTION--
You are an assistant that answers concisely and uses bullets for steps. If the question is out of scope, reply: "I don’t have that info. Here’s how you can find it:" and give 2 pointers.

Example 1:
Q: How do I rotate an S3 key?
A: 1) Identify service principals 2) Create new key 3) Swap usages 4) Revoke old key.

Example 2:
Q: What is TTL in Redis?
A: TTL is time-to-live. Use EXPIRE to set, TTL to read. If expired, key removed.
--END--

Variants to try:
- add a single negative exemplar: show a hallucinated answer and then the corrected short answer.
- force an output schema: prefix with "OUTPUT AS JSON: {"answer": string, "sources": [string]"}". Test truncation behavior.

Medium template (for structured tasks + examples):
Role: "Policy assistant. Cite policy section IDs or say "none". Keep reasoning under 40 tokens."
Few-shot set (3 items): each example shows question, brief reasoning, output with section id.

Observed failure modes (notes + rough frequency):
- style drift (30%): voice changes across long dialog — likely due to hidden system/context switches. Fix: reassert role every 6–8 turns or add short reminder at top of each system message.
- hallucinated citations (45%): model invents section numbers or fake URLs. Fixes to try: negative exemplars, explicit "If you cannot verify, say unknown" anchor, or require numeric confidence token.
- verbosity bleed (20%): assistant ignores concision instruction when user asks follow-ups. Try: token budget hint ("Answer in max 80 tokens").
- token-bloat in few-shot sets (non-linear cost): keep exemplars as distilled Q/A pairs — remove commentary.
- schema corruption on truncation (15%): when outputting JSON schema the model sometimes emits partial JSON. Fix: add closing sentinel string e.g., "<END>" and post-parse with safe fallbacks.

Failure-case mini-catalog (for prompt-registry tests):
1) Instruction ignoring when examples use different phrasing. Test: swap example phrasing to match edge-case user phrasing.
2) Overfitting to examples: model copies example phrasing verbatim rather than adapting. Test: paraphrase examples to encourage abstraction.
3) Repetition loops: model repeats last bullet twice when list framing ambiguous. Test: add "Do not repeat items" explicit rule.

Lightweight experiment matrix (priority):
- E1 (high): Compare negative-exemplar vs extra positive exemplar on hallucination rate across 3 models, 200 queries each. Metric: hallucination rate via gold-labeled answers.
- E2 (med): Schema + end-sentinel vs schema-only: measure JSON parse success and partial outputs.
- E3 (low): Short role re-assertion every N turns: N={3,6,9} — measure tone drift.

Measured heuristics to record (for each run):
- model, quantization, sequence length distribution, exemplar token count, hallucination rate, JSON-parse success %, average response tokens.

Small prototype few-shot bank (draft examples) — aim for 3 exemplars that cover typical variants:
1) Definitional question (short ask)
Q: What is OAuth?
A: OAuth is an authorization framework to allow apps delegated access. 2–3 lines. Sources: RFC6749.
2) Procedural short (steps)
Q: How to rotate a DB password with minimal downtime?
A: 1) Create new creds, 2) stage rotation with read-only, 3) swap, 4) revoke. Add one fallback pointer.
3) Out-of-scope case (should refuse and give pointers)
Q: Provide personal data for user X.
A: "I can’t help with personal data retrieval. Here’s how to request it formally: [link to privacy request form]"

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add automatic post-checker that marks answers with "confidence-low" tag when model used heuristics to fill gaps.
- Push E1 to CI and add an entry in prompt-registry with experiment metadata (link to PR above).
- Draft a short explainer for Solutions Eng on how to pick exemplars (keep it <1 page).

Unresolved questions (brain dump):
- Is one negative example always better than two positives for hallucination? My hunch: depends on task ambiguity. Need controlled test.
- How much does exemplar paraphrasing increase generalization vs cold few-shot? Anecdotal but not measured.

Quick references I want to keep handy:
- Confluence: Prompt Guidelines (linked above)
- JIRA-3421: prompt-registry schema changes
- PR 87: initial negative-exemplar implementation

Last quick thought: aim to make the prompt-registry support a compact attribute set for each template: {role_hint, exemplar_count, negative_examples_allowed, output_schema, end_sentinel}. If we standardize that, we can automate fail-safe transforms (insert sentinel, wrap schema, add short refusal exemplar) before sending to model.

-- end of aperture notes --

(These are rough; keep this file as source-of-truth for small experiments before I formalize.)
